query: How does Index stop stale source revisions from overwriting newer indexed data?

candidates.text: Index rejects upserts whose revision_sequence is older than the latest indexed revision. Revision sequences are monotonic per source, and opaque source revision IDs are never ordered lexicographically.
Gateway resolves the active Index generation once at the start of a query and pins all lexical and vector retrieval calls to the same generation and immutable profile digest.
Index stores a durable source-wide tombstone high-water mark and rejects upserts whose revision_sequence is at or below that mark, including delayed operations after restart or during rebuild.
Tokenization preserves technical identifiers and produces normalized lexical terms with stable Unicode code-point offsets under a pinned tokenization profile.

Index upsert operations are idempotent per target generation, source_id, revision_sequence, and index profile digest. Reusing the same operation identity with a conflicting canonical payload is rejected.
Ranking combines lexical and vector candidate lists using deterministic reciprocal rank fusion and does not compare their raw scores directly.
Embedding uses Nomic Embed Text v1.5 locally on CPU and prepends distinct search_query and search_document task prefixes.
Every Index generation is bound to an immutable profile identity and digest. Retrieval rejects incompatible component profiles instead of falling back to a current profile.
Chunking splits a source into bounded chunks while preserving source revision identity and structural line spans.
Index rebuilds create a separate non-queryable generation, replay canonical changes, validate readiness, and cut over only after owners confirm their change journals are caught up.
Lexical Retrieval calculates BM25 scores from term frequency, document frequency, and scope-specific corpus statistics supplied by Index.
Vector Retrieval orders candidates by the configured cosine, dot-product, or Euclidean metric and checks query vector dimensions against the pinned profile.
Memory retains a durable owner journal and retries or reconciles accepted source operations after failures between canonical persistence and Index persistence.
Candidate provenance records source identity, revision sequence, chunk identity, and the profiles used to derive the indexed representation.
Index applies canonical scope partitions to retrieval queries and computes lexical corpus statistics only within the selected partition.
Reranking applies a local cross-encoder to a bounded set of already-ranked candidates and preserves candidate identities and exact identifier evidence.
The Index source manifest reports indexed source identities and revision sequences to support owner-led reconciliation and completeness checks.
CE REST services return a common error envelope with stable error codes, retryability, and correlation request IDs.
All inference runs locally on CPU; model files are provisioned before startup and no service downloads weights at request time.
CE services propagate request identifiers and deadlines, bound retry behavior, and return explicit deadline errors instead of false successful no-match results.
